title: From sensor A to sensor B in Ladder
summary: Hold a belt on between two sensors: run the belt when sensor A sees a box and stop it when the box reaches sensor B.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Hold an output on between two sensor events without a separate memory variable.
Explain why a sensor that goes dark cannot hold the output by itself.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/LatchTwoSensors.ld.json the inputs EyeA and EyeB and the output Run are declared, and there are no rungs yet. A box starts in front of EyeA; the belt must start when EyeA sees the box, keep running after the box leaves EyeA, and stop when EyeB sees the box.
stages.checkpoint: You can say why the belt must keep running after EyeA goes dark, and what the belt must do if EyeA and EyeB both see a box.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow the box: sensor A sees it at the start, then the box moves on and A goes dark long before B sees it.
stages.checkpoint: Run turns on when A sees the box, stays on while the box travels, and turns off when B sees it, {{v:LatchTwoSensors.Run=false@8000|staying OFF}} at {{t:8000}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Draw the rungs, save the program, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program has no rungs, so the belt never runs. The belt must start when EyeA sees the box, keep running once the box leaves EyeA, and stop as soon as EyeB sees the box.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the machine move, press {{ui:toolbar.run.label}} (F5) and open the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named latch-two-sensors and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the box leave EyeA and travel to EyeB in the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}; compare the moment EyeA goes dark with the moment EyeB turns on in the trace.
stages.checkpoint: Both sensors count the box, Run stays on across the middle of the belt, Run is off at the end, and no box is dropped.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The scenario checks that both sensors saw the box and that Run is off at {{t:8000}} ms. What would happen if a second box arrived in front of EyeA while the first box was still waiting in front of EyeB?
stages.checkpoint: With both EyeA and EyeB TRUE in the same scan, you can say whether the belt stays stopped or moves, and which of your rungs decides it.

hints.text: The box leaves EyeA long before it reaches EyeB, so a plain coil driven by EyeA would stop the belt at once. The output Run itself can hold the state between the two events: one event turns it on and leaves it on, and the other turns it off.
Draw a rung with an EyeA contact and a SET coil on Run, and add a second rung below it with an EyeB contact and a RESET coil on Run so the reset wins when both sensors are TRUE.

faultCases: The starting program has no rungs, so the belt never runs.
